observation.text: The synthetic worker reports afternoon fatigue and difficulty continuing after dense back-to-back online meetings.
Falcon bootstrap material treats health-condition labels as condition windows, not as direct accommodation lookup keys.

inference.text: The useful provisional reading is a health-time and work-density contact-point problem, not a condition-to-accommodation conclusion.

counterHypothesis.text: The primary friction might be schedule unpredictability, meeting role ambiguity, evaluation pressure, or lack of recovery-time permission rather than meeting density itself.
wouldChange: next questions would move from meeting count to predictability, role, recovery access, and evaluation expectations
implementation conditions would route to manager scheduling authority and review boundaries before any support option

missingContext.question: What does the worker identify as the most difficult moment: fatigue, role overload, recovery loss, evaluation pressure, or another contact point?
missingContext.whyItMatters: The kernel must not convert a thin fatigue statement into a person-trait explanation before the worker-defined contact point is clear.

missingContext.question: Which tasks, decision points, and participation obligations are attached to the online meetings?
missingContext.whyItMatters: Meeting density has different meanings if meetings are information intake, decision-making, evaluation, customer response, or coordination work.

missingContext.question: How long is recovery time after meetings, and is short recovery time actually available in the schedule?
missingContext.whyItMatters: The hypothesis changes if the issue is total workload, meeting sequencing, recovery access, or end-of-day depletion.

missingContext.question: What meeting environment factors are present, such as camera expectation, interruption, sensory load, decision speed, or informal chat?
missingContext.whyItMatters: The same meeting count can have different functional meaning depending on environmental demands and participation rules.

missingContext.question: Is there a support route that can translate health-time information into scheduling, role, and evaluation questions without forcing disclosure?
missingContext.whyItMatters: Support is not valid merely because it exists; the kernel needs to know whether it can translate the issue into work conditions.

missingContext.question: Who can change meeting cadence, role expectations, break rules, or evaluation treatment?
missingContext.whyItMatters: A provisional insight is only actionable if the implementation actor and decision owner are visible.

missingContext.question: What would the employer, support staff, and any health actor say about the same meeting pattern?
missingContext.whyItMatters: Axiom must preserve source-lens differences instead of averaging them into one explanation.

implementationActorConditions.condition: Can describe which meeting moments produce depletion without being asked to prove a diagnosis.
Has authority to inspect meeting density, role assignment, recovery access, and evaluation expectations.
Can translate health-time and work-density information into questions while preserving consent and source-lens boundaries.
